characters.name: Plan Keeper Ivo
characters.role: Keeper of the island trial table

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: The dock crew needs eight crates before the shift horn in fifty minutes. Two early crates let them start bolting the new landing rail. Read Joss’s route card and the marks at Quiet Margin. Then take the ferry and another route around the trial table.

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: Both runs moved eight crates on the practice table. The time sheet shows when the loads finish. The other sheet counts marked quiet strips along each route. A strip can be crossed without telling us how loud it was.

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: Keep the first sheet dated. If the landing crew changes where the ferry ties up, ask Joss for the ramp slip. The draft line above this table assumes the ferry can load four crates anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: Move the landing setting to Lower landing. The ferry holds two crates on that ramp. Repeat the ferry and the route on your first sheet. If that was the ferry, take a second route all the way around too.

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: You kept the crate count and route rules while changing the landing. The ridge and marsh routes still use the same path. The ferry needs four runs at the lower ramp. Joss needs a new sheet for this shift.

dialogue.speaker: island-planner
dialogue.text: The checked line belongs to these two ramps. We still have no timing for a stalled boat or an extra wagon. The first and revised sheets at the dock leave room for another day’s checks.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Here is how much each load carries and how long a circuit takes. The ferry crew stays on the water and avoids the ridge slope. The marsh handcart takes the first pair quickly, then needs to return for more.

options.text: Leave the dock ready.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The trial gives us a last arrival and a crossing count. Our rail crew can start as soon as the first pair reaches them. A loaded cart on the ridge needs a steady pull. Put a tested route on the high-landing sheet.

options.text: Put the ridge cart on the upper-landing plan.
Load the ferry from the upper landing.
Send the first pair by the marsh path.
Leave the load sheet open.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Joss sends for the slope crew and their ridge cart. The practice route takes thirty-six minutes for all eight crates and counts two quiet strips. The loading spot stays open for the ferry if the plan changes.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Joss stacks four crates at each side of the upper ramp. The practice ferry brings all eight in twenty-four minutes and counts four quiet strips. The crew stays off the ridge slope.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Joss moves the first pair onto the marsh handcart so the rail work can start early. The first circuit takes ten minutes and all four take forty. The strip count reaches twelve. The handcart crew keeps the marker map nearby.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The ferry has to tie up below the main ramp. There is a new slip at the lower landing. Take it to Ivo and see what changes with the same eight crates.

options.text: Leave the dock ready.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The lower ramp changed the ferry load. The ridge keeps more time in hand but needs the slope crew. The handcart brings the first pair early. Choose a route you tried at the lower setting and leave the upper sheet beside it.

options.text: Put the ridge cart on the revised sheet.
Keep the ferry and record the smaller loads.
Start the revised run by the marsh path.
Leave both sheets on the dock for now.
On Glass Walk we checked the route from two approaches.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Yes. From the stair foot, the rail had a different approach. The ferry still follows the same course, but coming at this ramp changes what the deck can carry. Put that starting point on the sheet.

options.text: Put the ridge cart on the revised sheet.
Keep the ferry and record the smaller loads.
Start the revised run by the marsh path.
Leave both sheets on the dock for now.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The slope crew gets both cart loads. The lower-landing sheet shows thirty-six minutes, two quiet-strip crossings, and fourteen minutes in hand. The upper sheet keeps its former plan.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Joss leaves the crates at the lower ramp in pairs and puts a hand signal on the post for the next boat. Four circuits take forty-eight minutes, count eight quiet strips, and leave two minutes in hand.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The rail crew gets the first pair on the ten-minute handcart circuit. The board gives forty minutes for the full delivery and twelve strip crossings. The marsh handcart follows the marked edge.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Someone left a reply at the bend in Quiet Margin. They heard a cart there. See what their place tells us that the estimated strip count could not.

options.text: Leave the dock ready.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The strip map helped us keep track of where the route runs. A worker heard a rattle at one bend. If you leave a log, the next listener can mark where and when without giving the sound a distance we did not measure.

options.text: Put a place-and-time log by the quiet strip.
Keep the field note at the bend.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: Joss hangs a spare sleeve at the bend with a line for the place and time. The crate counts and strip estimates stay on their own sheets. Someone on the next shift can add what they actually hear.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The new sleeve is where the route turns. The first listener’s note is still there, beside the two lines they can leave for the next crew.

options.text: Leave the dock ready.
Check the square board with me.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: You saw the square raised while the swing rail stood open. The south-bank crews taught that wait signal to their apprentices. Crossing still depends on the person at the ramp. We can put a waiting line beside the board for new carriers, or keep its sightline clear and explain it at the shelter.

options.text: Put the waiting line beside the square.
Keep the square clear and leave the guide at the shelter.
Leave the signal as it is.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: A new carrier reads the waiting line at the rail and stands back until a hand turns up. Joss keeps the origin line on the same board for people who want to know where the sign came from.

dialogue.speaker: island-dockhand
dialogue.text: The lookout can still pick out the square across the water. A new carrier can follow the note to Joss’s shelter and hear when the ramp hands use it.

missions.title: The Eight Crates
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When does a change at one landing make the original route plan too narrow?
missions.stake: If the plan fails, the island's harvest fair has no crates.

objectives.title: Find Ivo at the island trial table.
Find the route card and inspect the marks at Quiet Margin.
Try the upper-landing ferry and a second route on the trial table.

kq.action: compare routes under the same loading condition

objectives.title: Put one tested upper-landing route on the dock sheet.
Read the new ramp slip at the lower landing.
Repeat the original route and compare the ferry with another route at the lower setting.

kq.action: change one loading assumption while revisiting the first route

objectives.title: Give the dock crew a revised sheet for the lower landing.

kq.action: publish the new loading assumption beside a dated previous estimate

missions.title: At the Quiet Bend
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What do people still need to observe after they count a route’s crossings?

objectives.title: Find the margin worker’s reply about a sound at the bend.
Leave a place-and-time log for the next margin listener.

missions.title: Wait at the Square
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a sign keep its local meaning when new crews arrive?

objectives.title: Check the square board against the rail and the crew’s practice.
Help Joss explain the waiting signal to new carriers.

journal.text: Eight crates kept their count when the ferry moved ramps. The number per circuit changed. We kept both plans and recorded which parts of the island each route crossed.

moments.did: You tried more than one way of taking the same load to the dock.
moments.prompt: Who needed the first pair before the rest?

moments.did: You repeated routes after the ferry changed ramps.
moments.prompt: Which part of your trial could you keep steady?

moments.did: You left room for a listener to record their own place and time.
moments.prompt: What can someone hear at a bend that a route table cannot show?

chronicle.title: Eight crates on the upper sheet
chronicle.text: The dock has an upper-landing plan for the eight crates. The trial gave a time and a count of marked quiet strips.

chronicle.title: A smaller ferry load
chronicle.text: The lower ramp changed how many crates fit on one ferry circuit. The revised route has its own sheet beside the original.
